edges.description: Diagnostic cultures can recover Actinomyces from Actinomyces-associated primary canaliculitis.
The microbial aggregates formed in the canalicular lumen are the canalicular dacroliths found during canaliculitis surgery.
Chronic infected mucosa and retained concretions enlarge the canalicular lumen and produce stagnant, obstructed lacrimal flow.
Canalicular inflammation and obstructive sequelae impair lacrimal drainage and contribute to tearing in canaliculitis.
Inflamed infected canaliculi can express purulent material through the lacrimal punctum.
Canalicular infection and mucosal inflammation produce medial eyelid swelling around the affected canaliculus.
Inflammation and edema of the vertical canalicular epithelium protrude the lacrimal punctum and make the punctal surface hyperemic.
Occlusion and stagnant lacrimal flow retain organisms and infected concretions, feeding the infection-inflammation-stasis loop.
Reduced tear clearance can leave the canalicular lumen more permissive to Actinomyces retention, but the cited cohort establishes coexisting dry eye rather than measuring the intervening flow defect.
Culture positivity reports recovery of Actinomyces species from the infected lacrimal canaliculus.

nodes.description: Resident or odontogenic Actinomyces organisms colonize the lacrimal canalicular lumen, often in an adult with dry eye and impaired tear clearance, and provide the microbial biomass that accumulates in the duct.

evidence.reference_title: Actinomycotic primary canaliculitis: Predisposing factors, clinical characteristics, and treatment outcomes.
evidence.snippet: Of the 201 patients diagnosed with primary canaliculitis, 22 (10.9%) were caused by Actinomyces.

evidence.reference_title: Actinomycotic primary canaliculitis: Predisposing factors, clinical characteristics, and treatment outcomes.
evidence.snippet: Among 19 cases (86.0%) of identified Actinomyces species, A. odontolyticus (43.5%) was the predominant causative microorganism.

reports_on.interpretation: Culture positivity reports recovery of Actinomyces species from the infected lacrimal canaliculus.

nodes.description: Actinomyces-rich, frequently polymicrobial canalicular concretions create a protected intraluminal bacterial community that acts as a persistent nidus for chronic infection and explains recurrence when concretions remain.

evidence.reference_title: Metagenomic Shotgun Sequencing Analysis of Canalicular Concretions in Lacrimal Canaliculitis Cases.
evidence.snippet: Canalicular concretions are polymicrobial with anaerobic and facultative, aerobic bacteria.
In 15 out of 17 canaliculi, concretions were found intraoperatively.

nodes.description: Canaliculotomy opens the affected canaliculus and curettage removes the Actinomyces-rich concretions that maintain the protected infectious nidus; silicone tube intubation during the procedure can reduce postoperative obstruction.

evidence.snippet: Surgical canaliculotomies allow complete removal of bacterial concretions which are found in the canaliculi for the most part.

evidence.reference_title: Outcomes of Canaliculotomy with and without Silicone Tube Intubation in Management of Primary Canaliculitis.
evidence.snippet: Canaliculotomy with curettage gives excellent clinical outcomes in the treatment of patients with primary canaliculitis and a higher success rate can be achieved when silicone tube intubation is performed during the procedure.

nodes.description: Persistent infection of the lacrimal canalicular mucosa drives local inflammatory swelling, discharge from the punctum, epiphora, canalicular dilatation, and eventually stenotic sequelae that further impair drainage.

evidence.reference_title: Surgical procedure of canaliculoplasty in the treatment of primary canaliculitis associated with canalicular dilatation.
evidence.snippet: Primary canaliculitis is a chronic infection of the proximal lacrimal pathway.

nodes.description: Dry eye commonly coexists with Actinomyces-associated primary canaliculitis and may predispose by weakening tear clearance through the lacrimal canaliculus.

evidence.reference_title: Actinomycotic primary canaliculitis: Predisposing factors, clinical characteristics, and treatment outcomes.
evidence.snippet: Dry eye co-existed in 77.3% of patients, whereas no obvious systemic factors were found.

nodes.description: Tearing is common in mixed-etiology primary canaliculitis; the Actinomyces-specific cohort did not establish a similarly high Actinomyces-specific epiphora rate.

evidence.reference_title: Primary canaliculitis: clinical features, microbiological profile, and management outcome.
evidence.snippet: The most common presenting symptom was epiphora, noted in 63 (85%) patients, and the most common clinical sign was thickening of canalicular portion of eyelid seen in 53 (72%) patients.

nodes.description: Selected cases can be treated without a canaliculotomy by punctal dilation, manual expression or microcurettage of concretions, and irrigation with topical antibiotics chosen for the cultured organism.

evidence.reference_title: Incision-sparing management of canaliculitis: an efficacious alternative to surgical management.
evidence.snippet: Ten (83.3%) eyes were successfully treated with incision-sparing modalities, and 2 (16.7%) eyes were treated surgically.

evidence.reference_title: Actinomycotic primary canaliculitis: Predisposing factors, clinical characteristics, and treatment outcomes.
evidence.snippet: Conservative therapy combining repeated canalicular expression and irrigation with susceptible topical antibiotics achieved complete resolution in 86.4% of patients.

evidence.reference_title: A "Clinical Tetrad" for Easy Diagnosis of Lacrimal Canaliculitis.
evidence.snippet: The highlighting clinical features were medial eyelid edema (n = 40, 100%), pouting and hyperemia of lacrimal punctum (n = 36, 90%), yellowish canalicular hue (n = 35, 87.5%), and canalicular distention and expressible discharge (n = 32, 80%).

nodes.description: Long-standing canalicular inflammation and retained concretions dilate the canalicular lumen and create occlusion, lacrimal stagnation, and self-perpetuating infection.

evidence.reference_title: Surgical procedure of canaliculoplasty in the treatment of primary canaliculitis associated with canalicular dilatation.
evidence.snippet: The accumulated concretions, together with the mucopurulent discharge, are responsible for a self-perpetuating cycle of canalicular stasis and infection for years

evidence.reference_title: Actinomycotic primary canaliculitis: Predisposing factors, clinical characteristics, and treatment outcomes.
evidence.snippet: The most frequent symptom was mattering without epiphora (77.3%) and clinical signs were punctal regurgitation of purulent discharge (100%) and expressible concretions (95.5%).
